messages.subject: how to add several point range plots in only one graph, to present the results from multiple model?
parts:
Hi all, 

I would like to combine all these 3 plots in just one plot, where I could have for each coefficient three point ranges, each one from each model. I think these type of presentation of multiple coefficient in just one plot is becoming quite standard now but I don't know how to so them with the terrific ggplot. I really appreciate any help. Thanks in advance! 


Antonio Pedro. 

limits1 <-aes(ymax=res1[,3], ymin=res1[,1])
p1 <- qplot(rownames(res1),res1[,2],main=expression("Fixed Effects Estimates From the Main Models")) + 
      geom_pointrange(limits1) + coord_flip()
limits2 <-aes(ymax=res2[,3], ymin=res2[,1])
p2 <- qplot(rownames(res2),res2[,2],main=expression("Fixed Effects Estimates From the Main Models")) + 
  geom_pointrange(limits2) + coord_flip()
limits3 <-aes(ymax=res3[,3], ymin=res3[,1])
p3 <- qplot(rownames(res3),res3[,2],main=expression("Fixed Effects Estimates From the Main Models")) + 
  geom_pointrange(limits3) + coord_flip()

pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(1, 3)))
print(p1, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1))
print(p2, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 2))
print(p3, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 3))

messages.subject: Re: how to add several point range plots in only one graph, to present the results from multiple model?
parts:
Hi:

Here's one approach to what I think you want:

# Convert the matrices to data frames, create some
# new variables and row concatenate the results
resDF <- ldply(lapply(paste0("res", 1:3), function(x) {
d <- as.data.frame(get(x))
d$category <- rownames(d)
rownames(d) <- NULL
d$set <- substring(x, 4, 4)
d } ), rbind)

# Plot
ggplot(resDF, aes(x = category, y = mean, color = set)) +
geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = upper),
position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
labs(y = "Effect", x = "") +
coord_flip() +
ggtitle("Fixed effects estimates from the main model") +
scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "orange", "forestgreen"))

There appears to be a relationship between the size of the effect and
the length of the pointrange; you may want to check into that further.

Dennis

Hi:

There is no pch value 30, so this code yields warnings; replace it
with a valid value and you'll be fine. You probably didn't map the
shape aesthetic before creating a scale for it.

ggplot(resDF, aes(x = category, y = mean, color = set, shape = set)) +

geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = upper),
position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
labs(y = "Effect", x = "") +
coord_flip() +
ggtitle("Fixed effects estimates from the main model") +

scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "orange", "forestgreen")) +
scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 24, 30))

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: how to add several point range plots in only one graph, to present the results from multiple model?
parts:
Hi Antonio,
 
That error message typically comes when there is some sort of mismatch in your data.  For example you could be using variables from different datasets that have an unequal number of rows.  When you see the particular values 79, 0, the zero is a give away that for some variable, there is no data.  That can cue you in to look for missing variables or misspelled variable names.  In your case, you use mean, but the variable is called mean.median.  ggplot does not find a variable mean, so there is 0 rows of data for that.  This code works for me:
 
ggplot(resDF, aes(x = coef.name, y = mean.median, color = model)) +

geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = upper),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
 labs(y = "Effect", x = "") +
 coord_flip() +
 ggtitle("Fixed effects estimates from the main model") +
 scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "orange", "forestgreen"))

Cheers,
 
Josh
